metaDescription: Five 40V cordless hedge trimmers compared on blade length, cutting capacity, weight, battery layout and which platform you are really buying into.
expertTake: The SENIX 40V 24 inch trimmer is our top pick because a full inch of capacity, two included batteries and a dual-port charger make it the most complete kit here. The MITLEX 20 inch is the value pick for small hedges and the lightest carry. If your hedges are old, woody and thicker than an inch, skip this class and use loppers or a pole saw for the heavy wood.
introParagraphs: A cordless hedge trimmer in the mid-voltage class is built for privet, boxwood and other ordinary shrubs, not for old woody growth. What you are really choosing is a battery platform, because the tool outlives the first pack and the next purchases follow the batteries.

This guide explains how blade length, tooth gap and battery layout affect real trimming, and why some kits ship complete while others are bare. The quick picks sit above, and the detailed reviews below show which trimmer suits which hedge.

products.name: SENIX 40V 24 in Cordless Hedge Trimmer Kit, Two Batteries
products.description:
The SENIX gives a 24 inch dual-action blade and a full inch of cutting capacity, matching the Greenworks and beating the 3/4 inch Ryobi and BLACK+DECKER. Dual-action means both blade bars move, which cuts vibration and speeds the cut, and the aluminum structure helps keep the long blade straight.

It includes two 20V 2.0Ah batteries and a dual-port charger, a complete kit, where the Ryobi here ships bare. The packs run in series to make 40V and are compatible with the maker's X2 series tools, so the platform scales into other tools.

A soft-grip rear handle and wrap-around front handle give control for tops and sides. Oil the blades, clean sap and store the batteries inside. It suits owners who want a complete, capable kit.
products.bestFor: Owners who want a full inch of capacity and a complete kit with two batteries.
pros: Full 1 inch capacity on 24 inch dual-action blades
Two batteries and a dual-port charger are included
Aluminum structure keeps the long blade straight
Packs share with the maker's X2 series tools
cons: Two 2.0Ah packs are modest for large hedges
Newer platform with a smaller tool range
Both packs must be installed to run

products.name: Greenworks 40V 24 in Cordless Hedge Trimmer Kit, 2.0Ah USB
products.description:
The Greenworks kit matches the SENIX on blade length and capacity, at 24 inches and 1 inch, and adds a stated runtime of up to 60 minutes on its 2.0Ah battery. The battery has a USB port, so it can charge a phone in a pinch. A rotating rear handle and three-sided wrap handle help vertical and horizontal cuts.

The real strength is the platform: the same 40V pack fits a very wide range of Greenworks tools, so spares and add-ons are easy to find. It is a single-battery kit, versus the SENIX's two.

Clean the blades and oil them after each use, and keep the battery away from freezing garages. It suits owners who want an established platform.
products.bestFor: Owners who want a wide, established 40V tool platform and a complete single-battery kit.
pros: 1 inch capacity on 24 inch steel blades
Stated runtime of up to 60 minutes
USB port on the battery doubles as a power bank
Established 40V platform with many compatible tools
cons: Only one battery in the kit
Rotating handle adds a mechanism to maintain

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 40V MAX 22 in Hedge Trimmer, Battery and Charger
products.description:
The 22 inch BLACK+DECKER is the simplest kit here: a dual-action blade, a 3/4 inch capacity, a full-length trigger and a state-of-charge indicator. At 22 inches it is slightly shorter than the 24 inch models, which means a bit more maneuverability and less reach.

Its 3/4 inch capacity is a notch below the SENIX and Greenworks at 1 inch, so it suits young growth. A three-year limited warranty is a good sign and the battery and charger are included.

Lubricate the blades and clean sap off after use. It suits first-time buyers with ordinary shrubs.
products.bestFor: First-time buyers with ordinary shrubs who want a simple complete kit.
pros: Dual-action blade reduces vibration
Battery and charger are included
State-of-charge indicator shows runtime
Three year limited warranty
cons: 3/4 inch capacity is below the 1 inch models
22 inch blade covers less per pass

products.name: Ryobi 24 in 40V Cordless Hedge Trimmer, Bare Tool
products.description:
The Ryobi is a bare tool, so battery and charger are sold separately. It has 24 inch dual-action blades with 3/4 inch capacity and a HedgeSweep debris shield that pushes clippings off the blade as you cut. A wrap-around handle gives control.

It is the choice for owners already on the Ryobi 40V platform, which has a very wide tool range. The capacity is below the 1 inch SENIX and Greenworks, so thicker stems stall it sooner.

If you are starting out, add a battery and charger before comparing cost. Clean the blades and store the pack inside. It suits Ryobi owners.
products.bestFor: Existing Ryobi 40V battery owners who want a 24 inch trimmer with a debris sweep.
pros: 24 inch dual-action blades reduce vibration
HedgeSweep shield clears clippings from the blade
Fits the broad Ryobi 40V tool platform
Wrap-around handle for control
cons: Sold tool only, so a battery and charger cost extra
3/4 inch capacity is below the 1 inch models

products.name: MITLEX 40V 20 in Cordless Hedge Trimmer, Two 2.0Ah
products.description:
The MITLEX is the lightest trimmer here at 4.3 pounds, with a 20 inch dual-action blade and a 7/8 inch capacity, between the 3/4 and 1 inch classes. A 180 degree rotating rear handle and a dual-switch start make it comfortable and safe.

Two 2.0Ah batteries are included, each good for about 30 minutes of trimming. The warranty is one year, shorter than the three on the BLACK+DECKER and Greenworks, and the brand is less established.

The shorter blade means more passes on long hedges, but less weight to hold. Clean and oil the blades, and store the packs inside. It suits small hedges and users who prize light weight.
products.bestFor: Small hedges and users who prize low weight over reach.
pros: 4.3 pounds is the lightest in this guide
7/8 inch capacity beats the 3/4 inch units
Two batteries with about 30 minutes each
Dual-switch start adds safety
cons: 20 inch blade needs more passes on long hedges
One year warranty is the shortest here

buyingCriteria.explanation: The tool outlives its first battery, and the next purchases follow the platform. A shared 40V pack saves money across mowers, blowers and trimmers. Greenworks and Ryobi have the widest ranges, SENIX and MITLEX smaller ones.

The tooth gap sets how thick a green stem can enter. Capacity assumes soft wood, so leave a margin for dry stems. The SENIX and Greenworks claim 1 inch, the MITLEX 7/8, and the Ryobi and BLACK+DECKER 3/4.
Longer blades cover more but weigh more. A 24 inch blade suits long runs and a 20 inch blade suits small hedges. The MITLEX at 20 inches weighs 4.3 pounds and the 24 inch models are heavier.
Bare tools exclude battery and charger. The SENIX and MITLEX include two batteries, the Greenworks and BLACK+DECKER one, and the Ryobi none.
A rotating rear handle and wrap-around front grip help vertical cuts. The Greenworks and MITLEX rotate, and all five have a wrap-around front handle.
Warranty is the best proxy for battery confidence. The BLACK+DECKER has three years, the MITLEX only one, and the others vary.

maintenance.why: Sap hardens on teeth. A light oil film keeps friction down.
Vibration loosens them. Loose bolts widen the gap.
Lithium ages fastest when full or empty. Store near half charge.
Clippings trap heat. A brush keeps airflow clear.
Exposed teeth are a hazard and nick tools.

faq.q: Is 40V enough for a hedge trimmer?
faq.a: For ordinary shrubs, yes. Capacity and blade matter more than voltage.
The one that shares batteries with tools you own. Greenworks and Ryobi have the widest ranges.
The 1 inch models cut green stems up to an inch. Dry wood needs a margin.

faq.q: Are two batteries better than one?
faq.a: They allow swaps on long hedges. Two 2.0Ah packs are not the same as one larger pack.

faq.q: Do I need a bare tool or a kit?
faq.a: A bare tool is cheaper if you own packs. Otherwise a kit is simpler.

faq.q: How often should I oil the blades?
faq.a: After every use, since sap and moisture cause sticking and rust.
